references.text: Abraham lifts his eyes and sees three men, the same expression ('lifted his eyes and saw') used when he sees the place of sacrifice in the distance.
Abraham rises early and looks toward the place where Sodom and Gomorrah lay, parallel to how he lifts his eyes and sees the place of the offering in the distance.
The Epistle to the Hebrews refers to Abraham's faith in connection with the sacrifice of Isaac, and how he reckoned that God could raise Isaac from the dead – which connects to the third day.
'The third day' is a recurring biblical motif; Christ rose on the third day, and Abraham's journey to the place of sacrifice lasted exactly three days.
Abraham names the place 'The Lord sees', linking it to his seeing the place from afar – God had appointed this place.
John 8:56 interprets Abraham's view of 'the place' in Genesis 22 as a prophetic insight into Christ's day of atonement.
